title: Floors and beds do not fit shops, warehouses or flats - and floor may not deserve to be a layer
description: Two related pieces of user feedback, filed together because they are the same underlying question. (1) 'The floor data in the middle is useless, it should just be a metadata field, not a whole layer.' (2) 'Wardens are also using this for shops, warehouses and flats they own - there too, floor and bed do not make sense.' WHAT THE MODEL ASSUMES TODAY: Hostel > Floor > Room > Bed, four levels, each a table, with tenancy attached to a BED. That encodes a hostel-specific assumption - that the rentable unit is a bed in a shared room. For a shop, a warehouse or a whole flat, the rentable unit IS the property, and the warden is forced to invent a fake floor and a fake single bed to rent anything at all. THIS IS THE LARGEST TICKET ON THE BOARD and should not be started before a product decision. It touches the schema (DESIGN.md 3), every property screen, the tenancy model, invoicing, occupancy, the dashboard, the PDF exports and the CSV import. It also needs a Room migration for existing installs, which is a hard constraint here - the warden's only copy of their data is on the phone, so this can never ship with a destructive migration. THE TWO ASKS ARE DIFFERENT IN SIZE AND SHOULD BE SEPARATED WHEN SCOPED. Collapsing FLOOR into a label on Room is the smaller of the two: floor is already display-and-grouping only, it carries just a label and a sortOrder, and nothing depends on its identity except grouping and the occupancy rollups. Making BED optional is the deep one, because tenancy is keyed to bedId - everything from invoices to the vacancy notifications reaches a tenant through a bed. A MIDDLE PATH WORTH CONSIDERING before a full remodel: keep the schema and let a property TYPE drive how much of it the UI shows. A 'shop' or 'flat' would auto-create one implicit floor and one implicit unit, and simply never show those layers - the warden sees a property and a tenant. That delivers most of the user value with no migration and no change to invoicing, and it can be reversed if the full remodel later proves necessary. Recommend evaluating this against the full restructure rather than assuming the schema must change. Related: LODGY-41 puts vacant/occupied counts on floor cards, and LODGY-70 adds an all-hostels room view - both assume the current hierarchy and would need revisiting.
acceptanceCriteria: Product decision recorded: collapse the hierarchy in the schema, or keep it and hide layers by property type
A warden renting a shop, warehouse or whole flat can do so without inventing a fake floor and a fake bed
Floor stops being a mandatory step in setup for properties where it means nothing
Existing hostels are unaffected - the bed-level model still works where it genuinely applies
If the schema changes, a real Room migration is written and tested against a populated v4 database, and no data is lost - never fallbackToDestructiveMigration
Invoicing, occupancy, the dashboard, the PDF packet and the CSV import all still work for both property shapes
The impact on LODGY-41 and LODGY-70 is assessed before either is built on the old assumption

history.note: Filed from real warden feedback relayed by the PO. Checked against the code before filing; findings recorded in the description.

DECIDED: property type drives layer visibility - no schema change. A hostel keeps the full Hostel > Floor > Room > Bed model. A shop, warehouse or flat gets a type that auto-creates one implicit floor and one implicit unit, and the UI simply never shows those layers, so the warden sees a property and a tenant. Chosen over collapsing floor and making bed optional because that would touch invoicing, occupancy, the dashboard, the PDF packet and the CSV import, and would need a migration on data that exists only on the warden's phone. This delivers the user-visible value with no migration and stays reversible if a real remodel later proves necessary. BUILD NOTE: the implicit floor and unit must be real rows, not nulls, so every existing query, rollup and export keeps working untouched - the change is what the UI renders, not what the schema holds. Tenancy stays keyed to bedId.

Starting, building the PO's decided option: property type drives layer visibility, implicit rows stay real, tenancy stays keyed to bedId. Note the decision's 'no schema change' means no structural remodel - a propertyType column on hostels is still needed, so this carries migration 5->6 as a plain ADD COLUMN with DEFAULT 'HOSTEL', which leaves every existing property on the full four-level model untouched.

Built the PO's decided option. A propertyType on the property decides how much of Hostel > Floor > Room > Bed the UI shows; the schema keeps all four levels for every type.

WHAT WAS BUILT. PropertyType (HOSTEL, SHOP, WAREHOUSE, FLAT) with isSingleUnit = anything but HOSTEL. Migration 5->6, a plain ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL DEFAULT 'HOSTEL'. The add-property form asks the type first, and for a single-unit type swaps the setup-by-floors path for a single monthly rent field. Saving one creates its floor, room and bed as REAL rows - HostelFormViewModel.createSingleUnit - so nothing downstream can tell the difference. Tapping such a property on the Property tab goes straight to its unit rather than a floor list (HostelListViewModel.openProperty, falling back to the floor list if the implicit room is ever missing, so a tap cannot dead-end). The bed grid renders as a unit view for these: titled with the property and its type, rent shown per MONTH not per bed, no filter chips, the tile reads 'this property' rather than 'Bed A', and LODGY-69's sheet drops the room-type line and names the property. Editing a single-unit property carries the name and rent onto its implicit room, since the warden can never reach the room form.

WORDING. A warden who owns a hostel and two shops was still being told they were 'adding a hostel'. The screens that now span every type say property instead - list title, add/edit titles, the name field, the save button, the dashboard and packet 'all properties' scopes. Genuinely hostel-shaped concepts keep the word.

AC5 - MIGRATION TESTED AGAINST A REAL POPULATED v5 DATABASE, not a synthetic one. Pulled the emulator's live database (2 hostels, 3 floors, 19 rooms, 50 beds, 5 tenants, 5 agreements, 7 invoices, 7 payments, 2 expenses, 1 credit), installed the v6 build, opened the app to force the lazy migration, pulled it back with -wal and -shm. user_version 5 -> 6, every table's row count identical, every agreement's rent, non-revenue flag and invoice count unchanged, and both existing properties defaulted to HOSTEL. No fallbackToDestructiveMigration anywhere.

AC7 - IMPACT ASSESSED. LODGY-41's floor cards are only reachable for a hostel, since a single-unit property never opens a floor list, so they need no change. LODGY-70's all-rooms view DID need one and got it: a single-unit property's tile was showing its placeholder floor label, so the tile now shows the property type instead. Both verified on device.

VERIFIED END TO END ON THE EMULATOR. Created a SHOP with an 18000 rent: no floor or bed step anywhere. Tapping it opened the unit - 'Corner shop / dukaan', Rs18000 per month, one tile reading 'this property', vacant. Let it to a tenant through the normal agreement form and it flipped to occupied and returned to the unit view. Database confirms the full chain exists as real rows - hostel(SHOP) > floor('-') > room('Corner shop', SINGLE, 18000) > bed('A', OCCUPIED) - with an ordinary tenancy keyed to that bedId. Downstream all correct: the shop appears in the dashboard property switcher, full-room count went 2 -> 3, vacant beds stayed 46 because the shop is let, and the all-rooms tile reads 'Corner shop / dukaan' rather than a bogus floor. The two existing hostels are untouched throughout.

453 tests pass, line coverage 96.82%, jacocoCoverageVerification green. Six new tests: implicit floor/room/bed created for a single-unit property and NOT for a hostel, rent required only for single-unit, edits carried onto the implicit room, and both navigation branches including the missing-room fallback.

NOTE FOR QA: I left the Corner shop and its tenant in the emulator data on purpose, so the feature can be exercised without rebuilding it. Docs updated - DESIGN.md 3 and 4.2, DATA-MODEL.md, USER-MANUAL.md 2, and a decision-log row.

PASS - the PO's decided option (property type drives layer visibility, no structural remodel) is built and verified on the emulator against a real populated database.

AC1 decision recorded (PO history + DESIGN decision log). AC2/3 created a SHOP with ₹18000 rent through the add-property form - it asked type first, then a single monthly-rent field, with no floor or bed step anywhere; the shop then opened straight to its unit view (₹18000/month, one 'this property' tile), never a floor list. AC4 the two existing hostels are untouched - full Hostel>Floor>Room>Bed model, floor list with occupancy summaries all intact.
AC5 migration 5->6 is a plain ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT 'HOSTEL'; user_version reads 6, no fallbackToDestructiveMigration anywhere in the source, existing data intact.
AC6 invoicing/occupancy/dashboard verified on device (shop in the switcher, occupancy counts it, let it to a tenant normally); the printable PDF packet rendered across all three properties without crashing - pulled it and confirmed the Corner shop, its tenant and the ₹18000 rent all appear (2 pages, 117KB); CSV import operates on agreement rows and is type-agnostic (covered by the passing suite).
AC7 impact assessed and correct: the LODGY-70 All-rooms tile for the shop shows its type ('Shop') instead of the placeholder floor label; LODGY-41 floor cards are hostel-only and unaffected.

TWO MINOR WORDING LEAKS (cosmetic, not AC failures, flagging for the PO): (1) a single-unit tenant profile still reads 'Room Corner shop · Bed A' - the bed layer leaks into the profile label; (2) the printable-records scope button reads '3 hostels' when one of the three is a shop - the property/hostel rename that reached the property screens did not reach this counter.

453 unit tests pass, line coverage 96.82% (gate 0.93), jacocoCoverageVerification green.

Accepted, and this is the one that made the app fit what I actually own. My shop is set up as a shop - one rent, no floors, no beds to invent - and it still appears in the room view, the reports and the backup alongside the hostels. I never have to pretend it has a Bed A.
